newsitem.title: USA: Luby's chairman resigns after CEO's suicide.
newsitem.headline: Luby's chairman resigns after CEO's suicide.

text.p: Luby's Cafeterias Inc. Chairman Ralph "Pete" Erben resigned Monday after the suicide last week of his protege.

Erben, who tapped the late John Edward Curtis to succeed him at the helm of the San Antonio-based restaurant chain, was not available for comment. A company spokeswoman said he has been considering retirement "for some time."
Curtis, 49, was found dead last Thursday in a San Antonio Motel 6, his throat cut and a kitchen knife by his side. Police have ruled the death a suicide.
Facing his first board meeting as Chief Executive Officer on Thursday, Curtis apparently was despondent over store closings and pressures of running the 226-restaurant chain, police said.
John Lahourcade, 72, who stepped down as Luby's chairman in 1996, was elected chairman and named acting CEO. The company has begun a search for a permanent CEO and president.

Luby's earned $8.4 million, or 36 cents a share, in its second fiscal quarter ended on Feb. 28, compared to $9.3 million, or 40 cents a share, for the year-earlier period. Results for the latest quarter were in line with analysts' estimates.
Luby's stock ended unchanged at $19.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
